pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Textbook instance of the S0237/S0239 registry co-listing pattern already validated as producing correct UNWITNESSED verdicts in prior batches.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: This is the exact S0237/S0239 candidate-register census pattern the task instructions flag as a recurring coincidental-co-listing source. A (H-KOS-Context-002 Avacchedaka) belongs to S0237's 'Family 1 (IDENTITY)' table and is ultimately consolidated into the Identity Law (S0240: ruled 'the same constitutional content' as H-KOS-Context-001, not as B). B (H-KOS-Fallacy-001) belongs to a different family: S0237's 'Family 6 (REASONING)' register lists INV-KOS-Inference-001/H-KOS-Reasoning-Separation-001 etc., with 'fallacy detection machinery' recorded separately as an 11th deferred ENGINE mechanism serving law 7 (S0239) -- a structurally different kind of registry entry (a deferred mechanism, not a ratified Identity-family hypothesis). Both are simply rows in the same 25-row census (S0237) and validation pass (S0239); no lineage_claims connect Avacchedaka to Fallacy-001 specifically.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row stating H-KOS-Fallacy-001's invalid-reasoning detection depends on, or is scoped by, the Avacchedaka delimiting-conditions principle would establish a genuine DERIVED-FROM/EXTENSION link.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Same S0237/S0239 register-co-listing pattern as RP0793/RP0831/RP0864/RP1015.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both are members of the same S0237/S0239 25-row candidate-invariant register, but in different families: a (H-KOS-Dialogue-001, Structured Opposition) is explicitly listed under 'Family 7 (CONTRADICTION)' alongside H-KOS-Contradiction-001; b (H-KOS-Fallacy-001, Invalid-reasoning detection) belongs to 'Family 6 (REASONING)'. a's own validation row (S0239) ties Dialogue-001 to 'law 8' (the contradiction-preservation law) and to the debate-pipeline mechanism, not to Fallacy-001. No specific merge/relation ruling connects the two.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If the corpus's structured-opposition (Vada/Jalpa/Vitanda) framework is later shown to be the formal mechanism THROUGH WHICH fallacy detection (b) operates (both are reasoning-quality safeguards), an explicit ruling to that effect would upgrade this past UNWITNESSED -- not found in the sampled rows.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Being co-members of the corpus's own 'Family 6 REASONING' taxonomy is a real but weak signal -- worth a P3b note that shared-family membership in this census is a distinct, deliberately-orthogonal evidence kind (closer to co-classification than to lineage) and should probably not by itself move any pair off UNWITNESSED.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: CO-OCCURRENCE group (G1210, 4 shared rows), same registry-co-listing pattern: S0237's 'Family 6 (REASONING)' table and S0239's reasoning-family validation-decisions table list H-KOS-Failure-001 and H-KOS-Fallacy-001 as two of nine sibling reasoning-family entries, each independently validated ('STRONG -> KERNEL, SURVIVES'). Being siblings in the same taxonomic family within a census does not itself establish a lineage or dependency between the two specific hypotheses (preserving failed-reasoning traces vs detecting invalid reasoning).
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row stating fallacy detection (B) operates ON the preserved failed-reasoning traces (A) as its input, or that one hypothesis was derived by generalizing/narrowing the other, would move this to EXTENSION/SPECIALIZATION; not found.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Both fully sampled (5/5, 4/4, no truncation). Same registry-census source (S0237/S0239) as RP0791 -- both pairs in this batch drawn from the same 25-row Kernel-candidate consolidation exercise, reinforcing that this census structure produces many superficially-co-occurring but substantively unrelated label pairs.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Same S0237/S0239 candidate-register census pattern as RP0791. Both A (H-KOS-Fallacy-001) and B (H-KOS-Intent-001) are two of the 25 candidates in the shared Family 6 REASONING table (9 rows), but the ten named compression-test clusters test each against DIFFERENT other candidates, never against each other: cluster 7 is 'Fallacy-001<->Failure-001 -> COMPLEMENTARY' (A paired with Failure-001, not B); cluster 8 is 'Dialogue-001<->Contradiction-001<->Revisability-001<->Intent-001 -> COMPLEMENTARY' (B paired with Dialogue/Contradiction/Revisability, not A). Their final validation outcomes also diverge: H-KOS-Fallacy-001 is STRONG, promoted to KERNEL (state content -> law 7) + ENGINE (detection machinery); H-KOS-Intent-001 is MODERATE, ruled ENGINE-only and DEFERRED ('its corruption already covered by law 6 + law 7 -- useful; not constitutional').
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a fuller reading of the reasoning-family register showed Fallacy-001 and Intent-001 sharing a dependency (e.g. intent-detection feeding fallacy classification), this could support a real relationship. No such link appears in the sampled compression clusters or validation rows -- they are adjacent entries in the same family table with independent dispositions.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Textbook shared-registry-row false positive: both are simply two of the nine Family-6 (REASONING) candidates listed in the same census/validation documents, resolved to different, unrelated dispositions.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both families' rows are 100% identical shared S0237/S0239 candidate-register census rows (the 25-item Family-6 REASONING candidate table and its validation table) -- exactly the coincidental co-listing pattern flagged by the task brief. The compression-test rulings (S0237) explicitly test Fallacy-001<->Failure-001 as COMPLEMENTARY, never pairing Fallacy-001 with Lifecycle-Reasoning-001. The validation table (S0239) gives them different, unrelated dispositions: H-KOS-Fallacy-001 -> STRONG, KERNEL(state law)+ENGINE(detection machinery), SURVIVES (law 7); H-KOS-Lifecycle-Reasoning-001 -> MODERATE, MECHANISM, DEFERRED ('the lifecycle stages are the operational process executing law 6; constitutional content already expressed by law 6') -- two of nine sibling entries in the same family table, with no cross-reference or compression test linking them specifically.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a later source explicitly tested Fallacy-001 and Lifecycle-Reasoning-001 together for compression/subsumption (as was done for other pairs in the same table, e.g. Fallacy-001<->Failure-001), a positive relationship might emerge -- but no such row exists in the captured evidence.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: See RP0818's note on the shared census cluster; B's confirmed merge is with INV-KOS-001 (a label not in this pair), useful for whichever pair actually covers B<->INV-KOS-001 in another batch.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: A (Fallacy-001, Family 6 REASONING) and B (NonInterference-001, Family 4 TRANSFORMATION) are entries in two DIFFERENT families of the same S0237/S0239 register census, co-occurring only by table membership. B's own row S0240 records an explicit merge ruling -- 'H-KOS-NonInterference-001 is the transition-form of INV-KOS-001 (Dimension Independence); they render as one law' -- but that merge target is INV-KOS-001, not A; no row connects A and B to each other.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If Decision 2a's full text (only partially sampled) also addresses a Fallacy-001/NonInterference-001 relationship, that would change the verdict.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Flagging for P3b: shared explicit family membership ('Family 6 REASONING', 'law 6') is a step above pure CO-OCCURRENCE grouping-noise and below a specific pairwise ruling -- worth a closer look at the full law-6 frozen wording (not sampled here) before finalizing UNWITNESSED at roll-up.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both are explicit co-members of the SAME named sub-family within the S0237/S0239 register: 'Family 6 (REASONING), the largest family (9 rows)' includes both H-KOS-Fallacy-001 and H-KOS-Reasoning-Provenance-001 alongside INV-KOS-Inference-001, INV-KOS-Justification-001, etc., all validated together under 'law 6' (S0239: 'Reasoning-family validation decisions (9 rows)'). This is closer than generic co-occurrence (explicit shared family membership with a shared law number) but still falls short of a specific pairwise ruling identifying these two particular items as identical, derived, or otherwise related to each other rather than merely co-classified siblings under one broad topical law.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If law 6's frozen wording explicitly states fallacy-detection is the enforcement mechanism for reasoning-provenance (or vice versa), a stronger relationship (e.g. EXTENSION) would be warranted -- not present in the sampled rows, which show only shared family/law membership.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Same H-KOS/INV-KOS register cluster as RP0825/RP0841/RP0872/RP0891 -- see RP0825 notes.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Group evidence is CO-OCCURRENCE only (4 times), both entries in the same S0237/S0239 register. The full compression-test list's item (4) compares Reasoning-Separation-001 to Pramana-001/Agent-001/INV-001 (-> DISTINCT), and item (7) compares Fallacy-001 to Failure-001 (-> COMPLEMENTARY) -- but no listed cluster directly compares Fallacy-001 (A) to Reasoning-Separation-001 (B). Both independently 'SURVIVE' validation (S0239) as separate registered items with no merge/subsumption recorded between them.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A compression-test entry (in fuller S0237 text not captured in this extraction) directly naming both Fallacy-001 and Reasoning-Separation-001 would override this default.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both A (h-kos-fallacy-001-invalid-reasoning-detection) and B (h-kos-relation-001-epistemic-relations-first-class) are siblings in the same Family 6 REASONING register (S0237/S0239, 9-row family) -- co-listed with individual validation verdicts but no row relates them to each other specifically.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a row explicitly merged or cross-referenced H-KOS-Fallacy-001 and H-KOS-Relation-001.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Only evidence is CO-OCCURRENCE (2 times) within the same H-KOS-* numbered hypothesis catalogue -- sibling-registry-entries pattern. No row connects invalid-reasoning-detection to structured-doubt specifically.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: Would be wrong if a later row explicitly derives structured doubt (Samsaya) as the mechanism triggered upon fallacy detection, or vice versa.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both a_rows_sample and b_rows_sample are the identical S0237/S0239 rows -- the Family 6 (REASONING) 9-row candidate-invariant census/validation table. This is the shared-registry-row false-positive pattern explicitly flagged in the task instructions (coincidental co-listing of two different candidate invariants within the same large census table, not evidence the two concepts themselves are related beyond both being REASONING-family invariants).
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row specifically deriving the fallacy-detection invariant FROM the Vyapti inference-warranting relation (e.g. 'a fallacy is exactly a violation of Vyapti') would establish a genuine DERIVED-FROM or EXTENSION relationship; none was found outside the shared census rows.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Same census cluster as RP0818/RP0830 -- flag for a consolidated P1 pass over the full S0237/S0239/S0240 documents.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: A (Fallacy-001, Family 6 REASONING) and B (Zero-001, tied to the Family 2/Special-Area-B 'Unknown != Absent != False' law) are entries in different families of the same S0237/S0239 census, co-occurring only by shared table membership; no row states a direct relationship between invalid-reasoning detection and the unknown-is-valid-state law.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row explicitly stating that fallacy detection depends on or implements the Unknown-is-valid-state law (e.g. a fallacy classification that resolves to UNKNOWN rather than INVALID) would establish real continuity.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: CO-OCCURRENCE only (2 co-occurrences). A fuzzy scan found a REFINEMENT claim on S0240 ('H-KOS-NonInterference-001 is the transition-form of INV-KOS-001...They render as one law'), but that claim's actual subject is h-kos-noninterference-001 (a different label, the 'a' of pair RP0862), not h-kos-fallacy-001-invalid-reasoning-detection -- it does not bear on this specific pair.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row directly relating h-kos-fallacy-001's invalid-reasoning-detection content to INV-KOS-001's dimension-independence content (distinct from the noninterference/INV-KOS-001 relation found for a different pair) would establish a claim here.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Same census-registry pattern as prior batches' S0237/S0239 co-occurrences -- confirms this registry alone should not be treated as evidence of relatedness between any two of its 25 rows without an independent connecting claim.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both families' only shared content is the S0237/S0239 candidate-register census (the full 25-row Candidate table and its validation-decision table), the exact 'large registry/catalog row' coincidental-co-listing pattern flagged in the task brief -- H-KOS-Fallacy-001 sits in Family 6 (REASONING) and INV-KOS-Agent-001 sits in Family 8 (AGENT), two unrelated families in the same census, with no cross-family SOURCE-CLAIMED row connecting invalid-reasoning detection to epistemic-agency specifically.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row explicitly deriving the fallacy-detection mechanism from the epistemic-agency invariant (or vice versa) rather than merely co-listing both in the same 25-row registry would upgrade this beyond UNWITNESSED.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both share source rows S0237/S0239's Family 6 (REASONING) census table (9 rows) -- again the flagged shared-census pattern. The census assigns them to different validation laws (fallacy-detection machinery -> ENGINE/law 7; INV-KOS-Inference-001 Observation!=Inference -> KERNEL/law 6), with no row connecting them beyond common family membership.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row explicitly stating fallacy detection depends on / specializes / was derived from the Observation!=Inference invariant would establish a real relationship.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: This is the one candidate in the RP0802/RP0840/RP0868 trio where the full family-6 text was not directly visible in the sampled rows -- recommend a targeted lookup of S0237's complete Family 6 (REASONING) enumeration before treating this as fully closed.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Same shared-census pattern as RP0802/RP0868: both families' only visible connecting rows are S0237/S0239. b is explicitly named in the visible Family 6 (REASONING) text ('INV-KOS-Justification-001 Nature of Justification (forbids Claim->Knowledge without justification)'); a (H-KOS-Fallacy-001, 'Invalid-reasoning detection') is very plausibly also part of the same 9-row REASONING family given its subject matter, but its specific census-row text was truncated out of the visible excerpt ('...the Validation Lay[er]...'), so no explicit DISTINCT/SUBSUMES finding connecting the two specific candidates was directly readable.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If the untruncated Family 6 census text or compression-test-cluster analysis explicitly says H-KOS-Fallacy-001 and INV-KOS-Justification-001 were merged, or one subsumes the other, rather than being validated as separate distinct rows within the same family, this verdict should be upgraded (most likely to SPECIALIZATION or EXTENSION, since detecting invalid reasoning plausibly depends on / specializes the general justification requirement).

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Same H-KOS/INV-KOS register cluster as RP0825/RP0832/RP0872/RP0891; note A and B belong to different named families (REASONING vs EVIDENCE) within the same register, reinforcing that they are distinct by design.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Group evidence is CO-OCCURRENCE only (3 times). The full compression-test list's item (4) compares Pramana-001 to Reasoning-Separation-001/Agent-001/INV-001 (-> DISTINCT) and item (5) resolves Pramana's source-role-separation naming internally (-> RESOLVED, no new row) -- neither names Fallacy-001. Item (7) separately resolves Fallacy-001<->Failure-001 (-> COMPLEMENTARY), not involving Pramana-001. A (Fallacy, Family 6 REASONING) and B (Pramana, Family 2 EVIDENCE) belong to different named families in the register and are never directly cross-tested in the retrieved compression list.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A compression-test entry directly naming both Fallacy-001 and Pramana-001 (not retrieved in this extraction) would override this default.
